operands.name: lineWidth
operands.meaning: thickness of stroked lines, in user space units (0: the thinnest line the device can draw)

w.text: Sets the line width used by stroking.

operands.name: lineCap
operands.meaning: shape at the ends of open subpaths

J.text: Sets the line cap style used by stroking.

operands.name: lineJoin
operands.meaning: shape at the corners of paths

j.text: Sets the line join style used by stroking.

operands.name: miterLimit
operands.meaning: maximum ratio of miter length to line width before a miter join is beveled

operands.name: dashArray
operands.meaning: lengths of alternating dashes and gaps ([]: solid line)

operands.name: dashPhase
operands.meaning: distance into the pattern at which to start

d.text: Sets the line dash pattern used by stroking.

operands.name: flatness
operands.meaning: flatness tolerance, 0 to 100 (0: the device's default)

i.text: Sets the flatness tolerance: how precisely curves are approximated by straight lines.

operands.name: name
operands.meaning: graphics state parameter dictionary in /ExtGState of the resources

gs.text: Sets the parameters given in a graphics state parameter dictionary (line style, font, transparency, soft mask, overprint …).

q.text: Saves the whole graphics state on the graphics state stack. Must be balanced by Q in the same content.

Q.text: Restores the graphics state saved by the matching q.

cm.text: Modifies the current transformation matrix (CTM) by concatenating [a b c d e f] to it: what follows is drawn in the new coordinate system.

operands.name: x
operands.meaning: x of the new current point (user space)

operands.name: y
operands.meaning: y of the new current point (user space)

m.text: Begins a new subpath by moving the current point to (x, y), without drawing.

operands.name: x
operands.meaning: x of the end point (user space)

operands.name: y
operands.meaning: y of the end point (user space)

l.text: Appends a straight line from the current point to (x, y).

c.text: Appends a cubic Bézier curve from the current point to (x3, y3), with control points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2).

v.text: Appends a cubic Bézier curve to (x3, y3) whose first control point is the current point.

y.text: Appends a cubic Bézier curve to (x3, y3) whose second control point is the end point.

h.text: Closes the current subpath with a straight line back to its starting point.

re.text: Appends a rectangle as a complete closed subpath.

S.text: Strokes the current path with the current graphics state, then ends it (the path is discarded; a pending W / W* clips with it first).

s.text: Closes the current subpath, then strokes the current path with the current graphics state, then ends it (the path is discarded; a pending W / W* clips with it first).

f.text: Fills (nonzero winding rule) the current path with the current graphics state, then ends it (the path is discarded; a pending W / W* clips with it first).

F.text: Same as f; kept for compatibility (PDF writers should use f).

f*.text: Fills (even-odd rule) the current path with the current graphics state, then ends it (the path is discarded; a pending W / W* clips with it first).

B.text: Fills (nonzero winding rule) and then strokes the current path with the current graphics state, then ends it (the path is discarded; a pending W / W* clips with it first).

B*.text: Fills (even-odd rule) and then strokes the current path with the current graphics state, then ends it (the path is discarded; a pending W / W* clips with it first).

b.text: Closes the current subpath, then fills (nonzero winding rule) and then strokes the current path with the current graphics state, then ends it (the path is discarded; a pending W / W* clips with it first).

b*.text: Closes the current subpath, then fills (even-odd rule) and then strokes the current path with the current graphics state, then ends it (the path is discarded; a pending W / W* clips with it first).

n.text: Ends the path without filling or stroking it. Used after W / W* to set a clipping path without painting.

W.text: Intersects the clipping path with the current path (nonzero winding rule). Takes effect after the next path-painting operator (usually n).

W*.text: Intersects the clipping path with the current path (even-odd rule). Takes effect after the next path-painting operator (usually n).

BT.text: Begins a text object: resets the text matrix and text line matrix to the identity. Text objects do not nest.

ET.text: Ends a text object, discarding the text matrix. Glyphs drawn with a clipping render mode are added to the clipping path here.

operands.name: charSpace
operands.meaning: extra space added after each glyph, in unscaled text space units

operands.name: wordSpace
operands.meaning: extra space added after each single-byte code 32 (space), in unscaled text space units

operands.name: scale
operands.meaning: horizontal scaling of glyphs, in percent (100: normal)

operands.name: leading
operands.meaning: vertical distance between the baselines of lines, in unscaled text space units

TL.text: Sets the text leading, used by T*, ' and ".

operands.name: font
operands.meaning: font dictionary in /Font of the resources

operands.name: size
operands.meaning: scale factor applied to the glyphs (the font size)

Tf.text: Sets the text font and size.

values.4: fill and add to clipping path
values.5: stroke and add to clipping path
values.6: fill, stroke and add to clipping path

Tr.text: Sets the text rendering mode: whether glyphs are filled, stroked, added to the clipping path or invisible.

operands.name: rise
operands.meaning: distance to move the baseline up (negative: down), in unscaled text space units

Ts.text: Sets the text rise, for superscripts and subscripts.

operands.name: tx
operands.meaning: x offset, in unscaled text space units

operands.name: ty
operands.meaning: y offset, in unscaled text space units

Td.text: Moves to the start of the next line, offset from the start of the current line by (tx, ty).

operands.name: tx
operands.meaning: x offset, in unscaled text space units

operands.name: ty
operands.meaning: y offset, in unscaled text space units

TD.text: Same as Td, and sets the leading to −ty (as -ty TL tx ty Td).

Tm.text: Sets the text matrix and the text line matrix to [a b c d e f]. Does not concatenate: it replaces them.

T*.text: Moves to the start of the next line (as 0 −leading Td).

operands.name: string
operands.meaning: character codes, decoded through the current font's encoding

Tj.text: Shows a text string: paints its glyphs and advances the text matrix past them.

'.text: Moves to the next line and shows a text string (as T* string Tj).

\".text: Sets the word and character spacing, moves to the next line and shows a text string (as aw Tw ac Tc string ').

operands.name: array
operands.meaning: strings to show, and numbers moving the next glyph back (left, in horizontal writing) by number/1000 of text space units

TJ.text: Shows text strings, adjusting the position between them: kerning and justification.

operands.name: wx
operands.meaning: horizontal displacement of the glyph, in glyph space

d0.text: Sets the width of a Type 3 glyph and declares that its description sets its own colors. First operator of a glyph procedure.

operands.name: wx
operands.meaning: horizontal displacement of the glyph, in glyph space

d1.text: Sets the width and bounding box of a Type 3 glyph that is a shape painted in the current color (color operators are ignored in it). First operator of a glyph procedure.

operands.name: name
operands.meaning: color space: a device or Pattern family name, or a name in /ColorSpace of the resources

CS.text: Sets the color space for stroking, and the stroking color to that space's initial color.

operands.name: name
operands.meaning: color space: a device or Pattern family name, or a name in /ColorSpace of the resources

cs.text: Sets the color space for filling (nonstroking), and the fill color to that space's initial color.

SC.text: Sets the stroking color in the current stroking color space (device, CIE-based or Indexed spaces).

SCN.text: Sets the stroking color in the current stroking color space; also for Pattern, Separation, DeviceN and ICCBased spaces.

sc.text: Sets the fill color in the current fill color space (device, CIE-based or Indexed spaces).

scn.text: Sets the fill color in the current fill color space; also for Pattern, Separation, DeviceN and ICCBased spaces.

G.text: Sets the stroking color space to DeviceGray and the stroking color.

g.text: Sets the fill color space to DeviceGray and the fill color.

RG.text: Sets the stroking color space to DeviceRGB and the stroking color.

rg.text: Sets the fill color space to DeviceRGB and the fill color.

K.text: Sets the stroking color space to DeviceCMYK and the stroking color.

k.text: Sets the fill color space to DeviceCMYK and the fill color.

operands.name: name
operands.meaning: shading dictionary in /Shading of the resources

sh.text: Paints the shading over the current clipping region (the whole of it, unless the shading has a /BBox), independently of the current path.

BI.text: Begins an inline image: its parameters follow as key–value pairs (abbreviated keys allowed), then ID, the image data and EI.

ID.text: Begins the data of an inline image.

EI.text: Ends an inline image and paints it in the unit square of user space.

Do.text: Paints an XObject: an image is painted in the unit square of user space, a form XObject's content is run with its own /Matrix and resources.

operands.name: tag
operands.meaning: role or significance of the content (a name)

MP.text: Marks a point in the content.

operands.name: tag
operands.meaning: role or significance of the content (a name)

operands.name: properties
operands.meaning: property list: an inline dictionary, or the name of one in /Properties of the resources

DP.text: Marks a point in the content, with a property list.

operands.name: tag
operands.meaning: role or significance of the content (a name)

BMC.text: Begins a marked-content sequence, ended by the matching EMC.

operands.name: tag
operands.meaning: role or significance of the content (a name)

operands.name: properties
operands.meaning: property list: an inline dictionary, or the name of one in /Properties of the resources

BDC.text: Begins a marked-content sequence with a property list (e.g. /MCID for the structure tree, or an optional content group with /OC), ended by the matching EMC.

EMC.text: Ends the marked-content sequence begun by the matching BMC or BDC.

BX.text: Begins a compatibility section: unknown operators inside it are ignored instead of being errors.
